question: Assume today is 2026-08-15. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park in August 2026, as it will be reported in the National Park Service's official monthly visitation statistics.

target.what: Recreation visits to Yellowstone National Park (all five entrances, Wyoming/Montana/Idaho, NPS-defined 'recreation visits') during the full calendar month of August 2026, as reported in NPS Visitor Use Statistics monthly visitation data for Yellowstone NP
target.publisher: U.S. National Park Service — Visitor Use Statistics (NPS Stats) / Yellowstone National Park monthly visitation report
target.cadence: Monthly; typically released mid-to-late in the following month (August figures usually posted in September)
target.caveats: Target period is ongoing/future relative to the 2026-08-15 cutoff, so only the first ~14 days of the month could in principle be observed, and even those are unlikely to be published. NPS distinguishes 'recreation visits' (entry events counted at entrances, not unique people) from 'total recreation

candidates.perspective: NPS Visitor Use Statistics time series for Yellowstone
candidates.hypothesis: August is Yellowstone's peak month and has a stable multi-year level and seasonal shape, so August 2026 should be anchored near the August values of 2015-2025 with an adjustment for the recent trend and any 2025-2026 anomaly. Role: supplies the baseline level and the variability band.
candidates.data_to_find: Yellowstone NP monthly recreation visits for every August from ~2015 through 2025, plus the annual totals for the same years (to compute August's share of the year). Also the monthly series for 2025 and any 2026 months published before the cutoff. Minimum evidence: at least 5 August observations and their annual totals.

candidates.hypothesis: YTD recreation visits through July 2026 (published around mid-August 2026) combined with the historical ratio August / (YTD through July) gives a direct, current-signal-anchored estimate: August = YTD_Jul * ratio. Role: incorporates 2026-specific level shifts that a pure historical average would miss.
candidates.data_to_find: Yellowstone YTD recreation visits through July 2026 (and June/July 2026 monthly figures if released); the same YTD-through-July and August values for 2015-2025 to build the ratio distribution, including the anomalous 2022 (flood) and 2025 years.

candidates.hypothesis: August visits = (forecast 2026 annual recreation visits) × (August share of annual total). August's share of the annual total has historically clustered in a narrow band (~17-19%), so an independent annual estimate constrains August. Role: an alternative route that does not depend on the 2026 monthly series.
candidates.data_to_find: Annual recreation visits for Yellowstone 2015-2025 and each year's August value to compute the August share; any published 2026 annual forecast or summer-season outlook from NPS, the park, or gateway-state tourism offices.

Role: an independent physical constraint and plausibility check on any estimate.

Role: constrains whether August 2026 is at, below, or above the historical norm.

candidates.hypothesis: Any 2026 road construction, entrance closures, fire/smoke episodes, federal staffing or budget changes, reservation/timed-entry rules, or America250 programming shifts August 2026 away from the historical relationship; quantifying exposure (closed days, closed entrances' typical share of visits) converts the shock into a multiplicative adjustment. Role: modifier applied to routes d1-d3.

Role: a cross-check and, if the park series is unavailable, a transfer route using the historical Yellowstone/Grand Teton August ratio.

Shared dependency on the YTD series with m4; failure mode is that 2026 August's share of YTD could differ from the two recent normal years.

methods.rationale: Starts from the 2025 annual total, adjusts it to 2026 using the year-to-date-through-July ratio, then multiplies by the mean August share of annual visits from 2025, 2024, and 2021. p77 and p78 are rounded secondary annual totals, so they add uncertainty; p105 is an official annual value. methods.rationale: Transfers Grand Teton's June 2026/June 2025 monthly ratio to Yellowstone's August 2025 level. Both parks are in the same northern Rockies gateway region and face similar macro travel demand. This is a cross-check because the analogue is a different park and month; Grand Teton's year-to-date was up while its June was down, so the signal is noisy. Failure mode: park-specific demand, fire/smoke, or construction could make Yellowstone August differ from Grand Teton June.

methods.label: m1
methods.rationale: Uses the most recent observed August (2025) as a stable peak-month baseline. It deliberately ignores 2026-specific signals, so it is a slow anchor and will be biased high if the 2026 softness persists. Included as a baseline for backtesting, not as the preferred route.

methods.label: m2
methods.rationale: Applies the July 2026/July 2025 ratio to August 2025. July is the most recent month and captures 2026-specific demand, including the reported July softness. Failure mode: August may diverge from July because of weather, school calendars, or construction timing; the July signal is also a single month.

methods.label: m3
methods.rationale: Uses the historical August / year-to-date-through-July ratio from 2024 and 2025, applied to the 2026 year-to-date-through-July value. Excludes 2021 because post-COVID travel and capacity patterns made that year's seasonal ratio less comparable. Shared dependency on the YTD series with m4; failure mode is that 2026 August's share of YTD could differ from the two recent normal years.

methods.rationale: Transfers Grand Teton's June 2026/June 2025 monthly ratio to Yellowstone's August 2025 level. Both parks are in the same northern Rockies gateway region and face similar macro travel demand. This is a cross-check because the analogue is a different park and month; Grand Teton's year-to-date was up while its June was down, so the signal is noisy. by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
